title: Set-Aside Accounts: Establishment at Closing and Limits per Loan
content:
**Rule.** A borrower may hold several Set-Aside Accounts, because one loan can carry a property-charge set-aside, a Repair Set-Aside and a Servicing Fee Set-Aside at the same time; there is no limit on the number of set-asides one borrower holds overall. What is limited is the same plan on the same loan: a loan never carries more open set-asides of one plan than the plan's per-loan limit shown in the plan matrix.

## Conditions of establishment

1. **One open set-aside per plan per loan.** A set-aside is established only when the same loan has no other set-aside of the same plan whose status is active or depleted. This is read from the set-aside records on the loan, matched by loan and plan, before the set-aside is established; what the borrower says about other set-asides does not replace those records.
2. **One LESA per loan.** The three LESA plans are mutually exclusive on one loan: a loan carries at most one LESA, whether Fully Funded LESA (Mandatory), Fully Funded LESA (Borrower-Elected) or Partially Funded LESA.
3. **Matching loan program.** A set-aside attaches only to a loan of a program its plan lists as eligible: HECM set-asides to a HECM loan, and the Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve to a Cedarline Summit loan.

| Existing set-aside on the same loan | Effect on establishing another set-aside of the same plan |
|---|---|
| Same plan, status active | Blocks it |
| Same plan, status depleted | Blocks it |
| Same plan, status cancelled or closed | Does not count against condition 1 |
| Any LESA plan, when the new set-aside is also a LESA | Blocks it under condition 2 |

## Opening funds and how the amount is set

- On establishment the initial set-aside amount is credited once as the opening funds, effective on the established date.
- The plan is set at closing. The Fully Funded LESA (Mandatory) and the Partially Funded LESA are imposed by the financial assessment, as the plan matrix records.
- The LESA and Servicing Fee Set-Aside amounts are computed to the age, set in the plan matrix, of the youngest borrower or eligible non-borrowing spouse; the Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve holds the plan's number of months of property charges.
- A Repair Set-Aside equals the plan's percent of the accepted repair estimate and may not exceed the plan's percent of the loan's maximum claim amount. It carries a repair administration fee equal to the greater of the plan's fee percent of the set-aside and the plan's minimum fee, paid at closing as a mandatory obligation and never from the set-aside.
- Only the Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve accepts additional borrower deposits, as its plan setting allows; a HECM set-aside is never added to after closing.

**Hypothetical case.** A HECM loan carries an active Fully Funded LESA (Borrower-Elected). A Servicing Fee Set-Aside may sit on the same loan beside it, but a Partially Funded LESA may not, because the loan already carries a LESA.
